correctness.rationale: For the smooth cyclic degree-three cover the discriminant is 1-2a^5 and Riemann-Hurwitz gives genus four. Direct coefficient extraction from F^7 and F^3 yields Cartier vectors A=(-a^5-1,-3a^3,-4a) and B=(3,3a^2,0), both nonzero on all parameters. The a-number is two. Using the correctly Frobenius-twisted Hasse-Witt products, the stable scalar is T=A.B^(11)=2a^25-3a^5-3; T=0 makes the third product zero, while T!=0 retains stable rank two. The exact factor T=2(a^5-2)G(a^5), with G(z)=z^4+2z^3+4z^2-3z-2, has irreducible factors of degrees five and twenty over F_11: gcd(G,z^121-z)=1, and G(0)=-2=9 is not a fifth power, so a fifth root of a root of G has degree five over F_11^4. Q(6)=10 prevents singular exceptional fibers. Both standalone verifiers completed successfully.

value.rationale: The explicit 25-point arithmetic degeneration scheme of a genus-four trigonal pencil is intrinsic and mathematically motivated. It is invisible in its entirety over the prime field, splitting into extension degrees five and twenty; the Frobenius-exchanged character spaces explain why stable rank drops by two even while the Cartier rank remains fixed. Unlike a routine substitution of p=11 into a previous p=7 formula, the congruence class of p modulo three changes the semilinear mechanism and yields a new irreducible-orbit structure. The result is a complete geometric marked-parameter classification, not a partial finite experiment or a known table recomputation.
